title: Prove launch touch reach deterministically, without dispatched taps

intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage: SEED-413#repair-refinement-touch-tap-hang at 686f3748df02795e7300a26695d1285b439efbdd

Verdict: Caught, by the earlier helper. The touch() check inside directionOpensBeneath was not the catch and never ran under this fault.

Promise checked: key example 4 and the goal "touch reaches each control". The Start session answer's direction toggle (`.project-actions .direction summary`) must open and close from a touch-reached activation. I used the suggested promise as given.

Fault (product code only; tests and fixtures unchanged): in dashboard/src/NearFutureDirection.tsx I gave `<section className="direction">` the style `position: relative`. I then added a sibling `<div data-fault="cover">` before `<details>`, styled `position:absolute; left:0; top:0; width:100%; height:44px; zIndex:5`. The overlay sits over the toggle's centre without changing any element's box.

Maintained check: dashboard/frontend-tests/launches/ad-hoc-start-session-answer.spec.ts, case "the refusal and direction retain their room when opened, closed and rotated by touch" (line 202). I ran it with the suggested focused command, one worker, in my own scratch worktree with Node 24.21.0 after npm ci.

Runs:
- Baseline: exit 0, 4 of 4 passed. The case took 487 ms.
- Faulted: exit 1, 2 failed and 2 passed.
  - The case at line 202 failed with `AssertionError: Near-future direction: expected false to be true`, from `expect(target.contains(hit), target.textContent).toBe(true)`.
  - That assertion is in controlsAreReachable (dashboard/frontend-tests/launches/launch-layout-page.ts:76).
  - The failing call was controlsAreReachable(row()) in wordsKeepTheirRoom (spec line 153), reached from spec line 220. That is the portrait call just before the first directionOpensBeneath.
  - The sibling phone case at line 187 failed on the same assertion through wordsKeepTheirRoom (spec line 195).
- Restored: exit 0, 4 of 4 passed. The case took 610 ms.

Independent observation of the wrong behavior: I ran a temporary scratch spec, not maintained and since deleted. It mounted NearFutureDirection at 390x844 and called document.elementFromPoint at the summary's centre.
- Under the fault, the hit was `DIV data-fault=cover`, and the summary did not contain it. A touch at the toggle's centre would land on the overlay, not the toggle.
- After restoration, the same witness hit the toggle's H2, inside the summary.

Scope of the claim: the browser hit test at the direction toggle's centre is the same centre hit that touch() uses. The maintained case catches a cover over it, but the catch comes from controlsAreReachable before the toggle is touched. The `touch reaches Near-future direction` assertion inside directionOpensBeneath was not exercised by this fault. Whether it alone would catch the fault was not tested.

Restoration: I reverted the product file with git checkout and deleted the witness spec. git status --short was empty, matching the clean pre-probe state, and the restored focused run passed. I removed the scratch worktree (/Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/39389266/tmp/intent) with `git worktree remove --force` and `git worktree prune`; it is no longer registered. I made no edits in the execution checkout and no commits, pushes or stashes.

Next proof action: none needed for this promise against a cover that is present all the time. Optional: to exercise touch()'s own message, use a fault that covers the toggle only after the row has been laid out. That needs a separate check.

Prior disposition: this matches the plan's intent that touch reach is the browser's hit test. It adds no new repair decision.

Costs:
- Test runtime (measured, from the Vitest-reported Duration of the focused command): baseline 2.23 s, faulted 2.26 s, restored 2.37 s. The two witness runs were about 2 s each (estimated; their Duration was not captured). Load average was about 13 to 21 at baseline.
- Human effort: unavailable. Nobody took part during the run.
- Agent effort: unavailable. Token and turn counts are not visible to this agent. Roughly 16 tool calls (estimated, counted from this session).

- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 98302 ms (measured), from 1795333718223 to 1795333816525 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

Wrap-up disposition: checked revision 686f3748df02795e7300a26695d1285b439efbdd; verdict Caught (controlsAreReachable centre-hit assertion); no follow-up.
